hero.headline: 73 Hickory Trail
hero.subheadline: A custom-built brick & stone home on a quiet cul-de-sac in Norris, TN

about.heading: About This Home
paragraphs: Custom built in 2006 with strong attention to detail inside and out, 73 Hickory Trail offers 4,600 finished square feet of brick and faux stone craftsmanship on a quiet cul-de-sac in Norris, Tennessee. The 1.08-acre lot backs directly up to TVA land, with quick and easy access to the watershed trails.

A graceful arch theme carries throughout the home — from the arched entry and transom windows above the main-floor doors and windows to the arched interior details. Every interior door is a solid-core Roman smooth two-panel wood door (no bi-folds, no pockets), and the Jeld-Wen Tenton desert-sand casement windows feature SDL fronts.

sections.title: Main Floor
sections.intro: Step through the arched front entry into a two-story foyer. The formal dining room sits to your left, the open living room straight ahead, and the master suite to your right — with the kitchen, breakfast area, laundry, and walk-in pantry beyond.

rooms.title: Foyer & Living Room
rooms.text: The two-story living room opens to the upstairs catwalk and fills with light from transom-topped windows. Iron balusters line the hardwood staircase rising from the foyer.

rooms.title: Formal Dining Room
rooms.text: Just off the foyer, the formal dining room, or music room as the original plans offered, is framed by arched openings and detailed millwork — an elegant setting for gatherings.

rooms.title: Kitchen & Breakfast Area
rooms.text: The kitchen centers on a large island with compactor and features a commercial-style separate refrigerator and freezer, six-burner gas stove with pot filler, and double wall oven with warming drawer. The breakfast dining area flows off the living room, and a separate walk-in pantry sits just beyond.

rooms.title: Master Bedroom
rooms.text: The main-floor master suite is a private retreat with generous his-and-her closets.

rooms.title: Master Bathroom
rooms.text: The large master ensuite offers his-and-her vanities, his-and-her shower heads, and abundant storage.

rooms.title: Laundry Room
rooms.text: A separate dedicated laundry room sits conveniently off the kitchen, near the garage entry.

sections.title: Upstairs
sections.intro: Cross the catwalk overlooking the living room to reach an open den, two bedrooms — one with its own upper patio — a bathroom with separate sink area, and a large finished bonus room with hidden extras.

rooms.title: Catwalk & Den
rooms.text: The catwalk spans the open living room and foyer below and leads to a bright open den — a flexible space for reading, play, or a home office.

rooms.title: Bedroom One
rooms.text: A comfortable bedroom with a double-door closet — and a secret door connecting to the finished lower attic playroom.

rooms.title: Bedroom Two with Upper Patio
rooms.text: This bedroom opens onto its own private upper patio with tile decking — morning coffee with a treetop view.

rooms.title: Upstairs Bathroom
rooms.text: Separate dual sink area with a private door to the bathroom and tub/shower — easy sharing for busy mornings.

rooms.title: Bonus Room
rooms.text: A large finished bonus room — being used as the 4th bedroom — with two separate attic storage areas and a finished lower attic featuring a secret door into Bedroom One, making a one-of-a-kind playroom.

sections.title: Lower Level
sections.intro: Downstairs offers a theater room with projector, a large living area opening to the pool, a full bathroom, a ventilated craft room (which could easily be a 5th bedroom), a fourth garage bay, and storage everywhere you look — including an under-porch storage room with steel door.

rooms.title: Theater Room
rooms.text: A dedicated theater room with projector — movie nights without leaving home.

rooms.title: Lower Living Room
rooms.text: The large lower-level living area walks straight out to the pool and patio, with a full bathroom just to the side.

rooms.title: Full Bathroom
rooms.text: A full bathroom serves the lower level and the pool — no wet feet through the house.

rooms.title: Craft Room
rooms.text: A dedicated craft room with an evacuation fan — perfect for projects that need ventilation — plus a large attached storage area.

rooms.title: Stairway & Lower Garage
rooms.text: The staircase leads down to the lower level, where a fourth garage bay makes an ideal workshop with drive-in access.

rooms.title: Utility & Storage
rooms.text: The utility room sits behind the theater, with additional storage under the stairs and an under-porch storage area secured by a steel door.

sections.title: Outdoor Living
sections.intro: A large in-ground salt water pool with slide and diving board, hot tub, pool house, and composite-decked patios — all backing up to TVA land.

rooms.title: Salt Water Pool
rooms.text: The in-ground salt water pool features a slide, diving board, and pool house, surrounded by a stamped cement deck and aluminum fencing with woods beyond. The Hot Tub sits between the pool and the house just outside the full bathroom door.

rooms.title: Patios & Decks
rooms.text: Multiple outdoor living spaces with composite decking overlook the pool and the wooded TVA land behind the property.

rooms.title: Curb Appeal
rooms.text: Brick and faux stone, arched windows, and a circle drive on a quiet cul-de-sac.

town.heading: Life in Norris
town.tagline: “The best thing about living in Norris… is living in Norris!”
paragraphs: Norris has been called a planned community, a model town, a garden city, and even a utopia. To its citizens it is a woodland home — an oasis apart from the busy world, yet only 10 minutes from Interstate 75 and 30 minutes from Knoxville.

The town has all the ingredients for comfortable living: tree-lined streets and sidewalks, a public library, outstanding schools, and a town center with its grocery, post office, service station, and restaurant. The 2,200-acre Norris Municipal Watershed offers miles of trails for hiking, horseback riding, and biking; the Clinch River offers great trout fishing; and nearby Norris Lake brings boating and water sports of every kind.

Planned and built by the Tennessee Valley Authority in 1933–35 to house the workers building Norris Dam, the town was designed to be fully electric, completely walkable, and wrapped in a buffer of protected forest — ideas so far ahead of their time that urban planners still call Norris “an American ideal.” Sold by the government in 1948 and bought piece by piece by its own residents, Norris has governed itself ever since — a bedroom community for Knoxville and Oak Ridge where the crime rate is very nearly zero.
